title: What happens in the two seconds after you tap your card
desc: Your tap travels down through four places and the answer comes back up; the money itself moves later. Read the numbered steps 1 to 14 in order.

sections.title: The journey of one tap

cards.name: You tap
cards.text: Your card meets the shop's card reader.

cards.name: The chip makes a one-time code
cards.text: A code that works only for this payment.

cards.name: The reader encrypts and sends
cards.text: It scrambles the details so no one can read them.

cards.name: The reader beeps
cards.text: You see the result and walk away.

cards.name: The processor formats the request
cards.text: The payment processor turns it into a standard message.

cards.name: The acquirer forwards it
cards.text: The acquirer, the shop's bank, passes it to the card network.

cards.name: The network swaps the token for the real card number
cards.text: A token is a stand-in number; the vault holds the real one.

cards.name: The network scores fraud risk
cards.text: A score says how unusual this payment is.

cards.name: The network routes to your bank
cards.text: The switch finds the right bank.

cards.name: Your bank checks the one-time code
cards.text: It confirms the code is genuine.

cards.name: Your bank checks balance and risk rules
cards.text: Is there enough money, and is it safe?

cards.name: Your bank answers approved or declined
cards.text: The issuer (the bank that gave you the card) decides.

cards.name: The money actually moves
cards.text: A clearing file and settlement between banks pay the shop the next day.

sections.closing: The answer takes about two seconds; the money follows a day later.

sections.label: It works like a restaurant order

left.name: In a restaurant
left.text: Guest orders; waiter carries it; kitchen pass; chef decides; suppliers paid weekly.

right.name: With your card
right.text: You; the reader; the card network; your bank; settlement between banks.

sections.link: order goes in, answer comes out
sections.closing: Same flow, with a bank in place of a kitchen.

right.name: Chip and PIN
right.text: Insert and key in a PIN.

rows.label: Who pays if it is fraud

rule.title: Phone wallet
rule.text: Proof: face or fingerprint. Shop sees a token. Limit: none. Offline: rarely. Fraud: usually the bank.

root.name: Declined
root.text: The bank or reader said no.

rows.name: Looks like fraud
rows.text: Unusual place, unusual amount, too many taps.

rows.name: Technical
rows.text: Reader offline, bank not answering, expired card.

facts.name: 4 parties
facts.text: Shop, shop's bank, network, your bank.
